# Incident Report — 2024-11-26 Traffic Analysis Exercise

## Victim Host

| Field | Value | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| IPv4 | 10.11.26.183 | Source of all malicious traffic; local RFC1918 /24 (10.11.26.0/24), gateway/DC at 10.11.26.3 |
| MAC | d0:57:7b:ce:fc:8b | ARP (`arp.src.proto_ipv4==10.11.26.183`) and Ethernet source on all frames from this IP |
| Windows hostname | DESKTOP-B8TQK49 | NBNS name registration `DESKTOP-B8TQK49<00>/<20>` from 10.11.26.183; confirmed in SMB session (`smb.native_os`/tree connect) |
| AD domain | NEMOTODES (nemotoads.health), DC = NEMOTODES-DC / 10.11.26.3 | DNS queries for `NEMOTODES-DC.nemotoads.health`, `_ldap._tcp...nemotoads.health`; SMB tree connects to `\\NEMOTODES-DC.nemotodes.health\IPC$`, `\sysvol`, `\Shared_Files` |
| Logged-in user | **oboomwald** | Kerberos `CNameString` field in AS-REQ/TGS traffic between 10.11.26.183 and the DC (10.11.26.3) |

## Malware Family

**NetSupport RAT** — the commercial NetSupport Manager remote-access client, abused as a trojanized RAT and delivered via a fake software/cracked-APK site.

**Attribution: signature-confirmed**, on two independent bases:
1. Multiple Suricata alerts fired directly on the traffic: `ETPRO TROJAN NetSupport RAT CnC Activity`, `ETPRO TROJAN Malicious NetSupport Rat CnC Checkin`, `ET INFO NetSupport Remote Admin Checkin`, `ET INFO NetSupport Remote Admin Response`, `ET POLICY NetSupport GeoLocation Lookup Request` — all tied to 10.11.26.183 ↔ 194.180.191.64.
2. Packet-level protocol confirmation: HTTP POST bodies to `194.180.191.64/fakeurl.htm` contain the literal NetSupport Manager wire protocol commands `CMD=POLL\nINFO=1\nACK=1` and `CMD=ENCD\nES=1\nDATA=<encrypted blob>`, and the HTTP User-Agent on every request is `NetSupport Manager/1.3`. This is the actual client-server handshake format used by genuine NetSupport Manager, confirming the tool rather than just a naming heuristic.

Delivery vector (behavioral): the client resolved `classicgrand.com` and then `modandcrackedapk.com` (flagged by Suricata as a known **ZPHP** — fake cracked-software/APK — campaign domain) seconds apart, immediately followed large encrypted downloads over TLS 443. The RAT began beaconing 34 seconds after those downloads completed, consistent with a fake-crack/mod-site lure dropping the RAT installer.

## Timeline (capture-local time)

| Time | Event |
|---|---|
| 08:50:11 | DNS resolves `classicgrand.com` → 213.246.109.5; large (~3.2 MB) TLS session immediately follows |
| 08:50:14 | DNS resolves `modandcrackedapk.com` → 193.42.38.139 (ET CURRENT_EVENTS ZPHP domain alert); large TLS sessions follow (~5.7 MB, 2.8 MB, 2.1 MB) — likely payload delivery, contents unrecoverable (TLS-encrypted) |
| 08:50:45 | NetSupport client performs geolocation lookup: `GET http://geo.netsupportsoftware.com/location/loca.asp` → response body `33.7488,-84.3877` (Atlanta, GA area) |
| 08:50:45 | First C2 checkin: `POST http://194.180.191.64/fakeurl.htm`, UA `NetSupport Manager/1.3`, body `CMD=POLL...` |
| 08:50:45 – 09:43:29 | Sustained C2 beaconing to 194.180.191.64:443 continues for ~53 minutes through the end of the capture (65+ POST requests) |

## Indicators of Compromise

**C2 endpoints**
- `194.180.191.64:443` — plaintext HTTP-over-443 C2 channel; evidence: repeated `POST http://194.180.191.64/fakeurl.htm` with NetSupport protocol bodies and UA `NetSupport Manager/1.3`; corroborated by Suricata `ETPRO TROJAN NetSupport RAT CnC Activity` / `Malicious NetSupport Rat CnC Checkin`

**Malicious domains**
- `modandcrackedapk.com` → 193.42.38.139 — evidence: DNS A response and TLS SNI from 10.11.26.183; Suricata `ET CURRENT_EVENTS ZPHP Domain in DNS Lookup` and `... in TLS SNI`
- `classicgrand.com` → 213.246.109.5 — evidence: DNS A response and TLS SNI from 10.11.26.183, immediately preceding the modandcrackedapk.com resolution and large encrypted download; likely lure/redirector in the delivery chain (not independently signature-flagged, so listed as behavioral)

**Malicious/abused URLs**
- `http://194.180.191.64/fakeurl.htm` — RAT C2 checkin URI, evidence: HTTP POST requests observed directly in the capture
- `http://geo.netsupportsoftware.com/location/loca.asp` — evidence: HTTP GET from 10.11.26.183, Suricata `ET POLICY NetSupport GeoLocation Lookup Request`; note this endpoint itself is legitimate NetSupport vendor infrastructure abused by the RAT for victim geolocation, not a malicious host

**Files / hashes**
- None recoverable. The delivery downloads to `classicgrand.com` and `modandcrackedapk.com` occurred entirely over TLS 443; no cleartext file transfer was captured, so no file name or SHA256 could be extracted from this pcap.

## Benign Context (not indicators)

- SMB/LDAP/Kerberos/DCE-RPC traffic between 10.11.26.183 and the domain controller (10.11.26.3) — normal AD domain activity (`\\NEMOTODES-DC\IPC$`, `\sysvol`, `\Shared_Files`). The `GPL NETBIOS SMB Session Setup NTMLSSP unicode asn1 overflow attempt` and `Potentially unsafe SMBv1 protocol` alerts are legacy signature false-positives on a standard NTLMSSP session-setup blob, not exploitation.
- Microsoft telemetry/update/connectivity traffic (`msftconnecttest.com`, `windowsupdate.com`, `smartscreen.microsoft.com`, `events.data.microsoft.com`, Office/MSN/Bing endpoints) — OS background noise.
- Adobe (`acroipm2.adobe.com`, `armmf.adobe.com`), Google (`google.com`, `googleapis.com`, `gstatic.com`), and CDN traffic (`code.jquery.com`, `createsend1.com`) — unrelated legitimate software.

## Incident Summary

The Windows workstation DESKTOP-B8TQK49 (10.11.26.183, MAC d0:57:7b:ce:fc:8b), logged in as domain user **oboomwald** on the NEMOTODES/nemotoads.health domain, was infected with **NetSupport RAT** after visiting `classicgrand.com` and a known fake cracked-software/APK site, `modandcrackedapk.com` (193.42.38.139), which delivered a payload over an encrypted HTTPS session. Roughly 34 seconds after the download, the RAT performed a geolocation checkin against legitimate NetSupport infrastructure and began sustained command-and-control communication with `194.180.191.64:443`, using the genuine NetSupport Manager client-server protocol (`fakeurl.htm`, UA `NetSupport Manager/1.3`), which continued for the remaining ~53 minutes of the capture.
